name: Closed enzyme-pool consistency repair
description: Find nonnegative E, ES, S and P satisfying two closed-pool conservation laws and an authored ES operating interval. Initial values deliberately violate both pools.
assumptions: Declared mechanism E+S<=>ES->E+P, with one enzyme moiety in E/ES and one substrate moiety in S/ES/P.
Fixed volume and closed moiety pools; no synthesis, degradation, transport or omitted bound states.
E_total=10 uM, substrate-moiety total=100 uM and the ES interval 2..6 uM are illustrative authored inputs, not measured biochemical constants.
q=(E,ES,S,P)/10 uM; normals and offsets act on q. Signed distances and tolerance use this normalized Euclidean concentration metric.
Pool equalities are conservation laws. The ES interval is an authored operating preference, not an additional physical law.
A feasible point establishes consistency with these constraints; repair is not a simulated reaction trajectory, kinetic prediction or experimental result.
This does not impose closed hydrogen-ion conservation on a buffered-pH biochemical system or supply complete elemental/charge balance.
One explicit feasible witness in physical coordinates is [7,3,77,20].
